feedback.problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions to the equation  $5\operatorname{cot}⁡x=11+\operatorname{cot}⁡x$ for ${0}^{∘}\le x<{360}^{∘},$ what is the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2},$ rounded to the nearest integer?
feedback.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange the equation and isolate $\operatorname{cot}⁡x$:

$$
\begin{aligned}5\operatorname{cot}⁡x & =11+\operatorname{cot}⁡x \\ 4\operatorname{cot}⁡x & =11 \\ \operatorname{cot}⁡x & =\frac{11}{4}\end{aligned}
$$

Recall that $\operatorname{cot}⁡x=\frac{1}{\operatorname{tan}⁡x}.$ Therefore, the given equation is equivalent to

$$
\operatorname{tan}⁡x=\frac{4}{11}
$$

Now, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\text{arctan}(\frac{4}{11})=(19.983\,1…)^{∘}≈{19.983}^{∘}\end{aligned}
$$

Since ${19.983}^{∘}$ lies inside the given domain, our first solution is ${x}_{1}={19.983}^{∘}.$

To generate more solutions, we add integer multiples of ${180}^{∘}.$ Hence,

$$
{x}_{2}={180}^{∘}+x={180}^{∘}+{19.983}^{∘}={199.983}^{∘}.
$$

Finally, the numerical value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ is

$$
19.983\cdot 199.983≈3\,996
$$

rounded to the nearest integer.
